description.p: The MorphologyFX class performs "fattening" or "thinning" of artwork. It is particularly useful for fattening or thinning an alpha channel.

The dilation (or erosion) kernel is a rectangle with a width of 2 * RadiusX and a height of 2 * RadiusY. The radii are measured in the filter's primitive units, so they follow the transform of the filtered vector and, when VectorFilter.PrimitiveUnits is BOUNDING_BOX, the size of its bounding box. Each radius is converted to whole pixels by truncation after scaling.

In dilation, the output pixel is the individual component-wise maximum of the corresponding R,G,B,A values in the input image's kernel rectangle. In erosion, the output pixel is the individual component-wise minimum of the corresponding R,G,B,A values in the input image's kernel rectangle.

Frequently this operation will take place on alpha-only images, such as that produced by the built-in input, SourceAlpha. In that case, the implementation might want to optimize the single channel case.
Because the algorithm operates on premultiplied colour values, it will always result in colour values less than or equal to the alpha channel.

action.name: Draw
action.comment: Render the effect to the target bitmap.
action.prototype: ERR acDraw(*Object, DOUBLE X, DOUBLE Y, DOUBLE Width, DOUBLE Height)

input.param: The X position of the region to be drawn.
The Y position of the region to be drawn.
The width of the region to be drawn.
The height of the region to be drawn.

field.name: Operator
field.comment: Set to either ERODE or DILATE.

description.p: The horizontal radius of the kernel, in the filter's primitive units. Fractional values are permitted. A value of zero disables the effect on this axis; the input is copied unchanged if both radii resolve to less than one pixel.

The vertical radius of the kernel, in the filter's primitive units. Fractional values are permitted. A value of zero disables the effect on this axis; the input is copied unchanged if both radii resolve to less than one pixel.

field.name: XMLDef
field.comment: Returns an SVG compliant XML string that describes the effect.
